notes.title: July Update
notes.notes:
[p]Hi Folks,[/p][p][/p][p]Just posting a small update as it's been a couple of months since the last.[/p][p]After the playtest back in Feb I realised there were a few fundamental things i needed to fix mainly around performance.[/p][p]I went back to the drawing board on a few things and have rebuilt some core systems from the ground up. I’d originally intended for the world to be made up of separate interconnected scenes with hard loading screens. I was going to design the gameplay such that these zone transitions wouldn't happen that often. But I knew nothing of memory management and how to load assets efficiently without causing stuttering during gameplay.[/p][p]Over the past months I've reworked the core world systems to stream assets efficiently and load and unload assets as the player moves around the world.
[/p][p][b]What does that mean for the game?[/b][/p][p]It will be a large open world game with minimal hard scene loads. I can't promise that there might be a spinner and maybe a fade on lower spec machines, but overall it should hopefully feel more open and immersive - that's what I'm aiming for anyway.[/p][p]Much of the previous gameplay systems work was good on the whole - combat inventory quests dialogue all good for the most part.
[/p][p][b]So what now?[/b][/p][p]After this large refactor I'm beginning to reach a point where things are starting to stabilize and I'm again turning to refining gameplay loops and building out content.[/p][p]I'm also starting to plan towards another playtest - this time with much of the previous feedback addressed and much more of the world to explore.
[/p][p][b]In summary:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Still here working away - having learned a lot over the past few months[/p][/*][*][p]A lot to do but going well[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Until next time[/p][p]J [/p]

notes.title: Devlog: April Update
notes.notes:
[b]Hi folks,[/b]

[b]Here's a quick update on things I’ve been focusing on over the past few weeks:[/b]

Mostly under-the-hood work this month. A lot of time went into refactoring the player controller and streamlining asset handling, which should help with load times and general stability. I also fixed a few long-standing performance issues — nothing flashy, but it clears the way for smoother play and cleaner iteration moving forward.

On the world-building side, small bits of the environment are starting to take shape. Nothing final yet, but the foundations are there and it's starting to feel like a place.

More soon

J

notes.title: Devlog: March Update
notes.notes:
[b]Hi folks,[/b]

[b]Here's a quick update on things I’ve been focusing on over the past few weeks:[/b]

[h3]Building the Character UI Screen[/h3]

I’ve been mainly working on the character UI screen. While the game is first-person, the character menu will provide a full view of the player character and their currently-equipped armour and weapons. I’ve been setting up the visible armor on the player’s arms in first-person view and syncing this in the character UI. I’m also adjusting the design to allow equipping armor, with stat changes displayed, and making it all gamepad-compatible. I'm also continuing to explore what can be achieved with character customization at the start of the game.

[h3]Refactors to Core Systems for Scalability[/h3]

As part of the work for the character UI I’ve also been refactoring the player character controller: cleaning up old code, updating animations, and integrating the final set of weapons and animations. Spells are next to be added. I kind of felt this had become essential at this point as the game scales to help keep things organized and easier to scale -  hopefully managing some of the complexity as the project grows.

[h3]Expanding the World[/h3]

In parallel to the above work I’ve begun building out more areas of the world and expanding the main questline. Feedback from the playtest was that the world generally looked good but I’d like to see what can be improved for free to improve immersion without impacting performance.

[h3]Ultra-Wide Support[/h3]

As I work mainly on a laptop, ultra-wide aspect ratios was something I completely overlooked. In response to this I’ve been working on UI adjustments to ensure full support for ultra-wide aspect ratios.

[h3]Performance & Stability[/h3]

Lastly, performance and stability remain top priorities. As I build out the game world I’ve been looking at ways to better organize settlements for easier loading and optimization using the tools that Unity provides. For those that are familiar with Unity I’m also working on refactoring the AI game entities i.e. enemies, NPCs and animals to use DOTs. more on this in future updates.

That’s it for this update.

Until next time.
J

notes.title: Update - New Gameplay Trailer and new Demo coming soon
notes.notes:
Outwith is a first-person single player open-world RPG set in a fantasy medieval world of lore and magic.

You're free to experience the world as you wish:

[list]
[*] Wander off the beaten path to explore
[*] Go anywhere and talk to anyone and 
[*] pick up side quests.
[*] Or simply follow the main story
[/list]

I’m essentially just working on the demo atm this will soon be released on Steam - early January.
Although it’s currently available on Itch.io should you wish to play it there before it becomes available on Steam.

[h3]About the Demo[/h3]

The demo includes the first main area. Access to the rest of the world is conveniently blocked by rockfalls which the villagers are diligently attempting to clear.

There’s one main questline - a take on the typical fetch a potion quest but with some unique differences.

The demo is designed to give a taste of many of the core gameplay features - hopefully it does the job.

[h3]A Rough Road Map[/h3]

My plan is to keep going on the demo refining core features. And during January I plan to work on improving the magic system adding more variety to the spells and integrating the VFX with the enemies.

Once the demo is out and February Steam Next Fest is over I’ll continue building out the rest of the game world.

The demo doesn’t include any character creation. I’m still working on this and it will be the first thing I focus on after Next Fest is over. Part of this work will cover adding full armour slots - head, hands, chest, legs and feet. And also re-evaluating the current NPC models.

I’ve also made some progress with the main story and world building. I’m likely going to scrap the previously-mentioned factions. Although There’ll still be choices and alliances. I’ve been working on the dialogue and quest system to support this - making things more manageable as the world and the complexity of the project grows.

I’m really grateful to everyone that has supported me and provided feedback. I’ve also made it easier to give feedback directly from the game - there’s now a link to a subforum on the Outwith store page on steam and my email address is there too.

So as mentioned my main focus has been getting the demo done and launched on Steam ready for the next Next Fest in February.

The longer term aim is to apply what I’ve implemented in the demo to the rest of the game world and build out the main quest line and other content with a tentative Early Access release set for this time next year.

[h3]About the magic system[/h3]

Magic is unlocked in the game by exploring and discovering artifacts which unlock a particular school of magic. Once a school has been unlocked you can use ability points to unlock individual spells in that category. You can also use ability points to unlock skills should you wish.

I did have classes in the game early on and they still exist in code. Although I’m considering leaving them out as it will make balancing the gameplay more manageable. Reasoning being that I’m prioritising balanced gameplay over having classes. Although as with anything it could change based on player feedback.

[h3]A fine example of premature optimisation - making interiors separate scenes[/h3]

One day in November I decided that it would help performance if I made all the interiors separate scenes and the player would encounter a hard loading screen when entering a building. This was supposed to reduce loading times for the main scene and help with fps.

Well after a few weeks of living with this, it turns out it made no difference and in fact made gameplay tedious when following the demo quest - enter house - loading screen - exit house - loading screen - enter tavern - loading screen - exit tavern - loading scree… you get the idea.

I’ve done away with the separate scenes for the interiors now and performance and loading times are unaffected. You can now walk through a door and you’re in a stranger’s house and they don’t mind at all - perfect.

The game world is constructed by linking separate scenes in Unity so there will be loading screens between main areas but I’m working toward this not happening too often during typical game play as the main areas will be large.

Which leads me onto fast travel. I’m working on this being integrated and making sense within the game world so it could be something like mage teleportation, bind and recall spells or horse and cart. I do like games where you have to think and plan your journey instead of just fast travelling on a map location marker. I feel the latter can lead to lots of loading screens. It may lead to a slower pace of play but hopefully will add to the immersion. Again, player feedback will tell.

There’s been so many updates over the past few months - some major highlights include:

[list]
[*] Improving archery
[*] Improving combat
[*] Implementing the UI
[*] Creating a settings menu
[/list]

That’s pretty much it for this update. One final reminder, the demo is currently available on Itch.io should you wish to check it out there. And please do reach out should you have any questions or feedback.

All the best 
Jeff

notes.title: Monthly Update #2
notes.notes:
This last month I've been mainly working on getting the UI in shape and doubling down on performance. Hopefully there should be some noticeable improvements for players in these two areas.

And one of the most crucial features in any RPG - finally animated the chest lids when opening for looting. There always seemed to be something else to do before this but now it's done I'm so happy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45171314/6684df9f9a903127c2c4cd3ea3adf873e971650a.png[/img]

Talking of satisfying details I've made the NPCs rotate to face the player. Sometimes in the middle of the night when I can't sleep I get up and try this out.

I've stripped out the other NPC dialogue animations for now - honestly they looked like they were doing some weird dance - all very odd.

[h2]Other updates this month include:[/h2]

Started extracting out settings - they're now available from the pause menu. [b]Notably added a toggle for gore.[/b]

Turned the hit effect from red blood to black blood for skeletons - doesn't make sense to have red blood. TBH doesn’t really make sense for them to have blood at all. The gore is volumetric and imho quite OTT and the performance isn't the best either so may look for an alternative effect.

Made some tweaks to the combat - enemies may wait to attack if your guard is up depending on how sneaky they are.

Oh and I added a compass too with points of interest and quest objective markers. And made the hud status bars auto hide too.

You can also drop inventory items all over the floor if you wish. And added weight although it's not that important for the demo as there aren’t loads of heavy items. I also tweaked the enemies to drop less, but more useful, loot items.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45171314/e8748a3579fac8d88166a386c202a4a20687d8b3.png[/img]

Final thing worth a mention - I fixed a spectacular bug where NPCs would disappear during dialogue if transitioning between day and night.

[h2]What's next?[/h2]

I hear you ask

Basically polishing anything that will fall under the scope of the demo and the next Next Fest event.

[list]
[*] Improving dialogue adding lore.
[*] Also revisiting the existing magic VFX and mechanics.
[*] Continuing to improve melee combat and combat in general.
[/list]

Look out for the demo coming soon.

Until next time
Jeff

notes.title: Monthly Update #1
notes.notes:
I'm going to try and start posting monthly updates here from now on and see how that goes.

My main focus at the moment is to get the demo polished for the upcoming Steam Next Fest in February 2025.

Working on the demo gives me a great opportunity to polish and refine some of the core mechanics and gather valuable feedback as the game progresses and before committing to some of the larger areas of the world building.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45171314/0424639c97a5f421e19cc882e4d707942bb77a6f.png[/img]

The demo will show the starting zone and a quest with multiple tasks which should give a good taster and feel for some of the game's core mechanics. There's a variety of enemies to deal with and a decent amount of interaction and exploration.

[h2]So it's a monthly update - What have I been up to?[/h2]

Basically continuing with the UI refining functionality and fixing issues. I was going for a grunge feel but now I'm challenged with making it feel coherent - form follows function and all that.

[h2]Here's a few of the other things I've been working on:[/h2]

[list]
[*] Worldbuilding - adding more lore, tweaking dialogue, writing new quests, adding to the main story.
[*] Optimisations - Optimising enemy models, establishing a base set of enemies and their distinct behaviour
[*] Tweaking melee combat - refactoring and tweaking timing, speed, camera movement, enemy detection. I've heard people say to establish a gameplay mechanic early on in the process, then build your game around that. Developing the sword and ranged magic combat was the first thing I did on this project. Nearly three years later I'm still working on it and will probably never stop tweaking it.
[*] Developing the magic system - integrating it with the world making it relevant and meaningful and setting up the UI.
[*] Improving the map system.
[*] Bug fixes - the update will never not be bug fixes
[/list]

[h2]Motivations:[/h2]

I'm a solo developer working on this game. I've been developing games in my spare time for years now and felt like it was time I made the game I really always wanted to play. 

I joke about getting fed up waiting for ES6 so I started making this game but there's a lot of truth in that. The game is very much inspired by the Elder Scrolls games, especially Morrowind and Skyrim. I’m the guy that never shuts up about Morrowind ːsteamhappyː

That's all for this week - until next time.
J
